title: Holistic Scaling Laws for Optimal Mixture-of-Experts Architecture Optimization
claim: A huge search space is cut step by step through constraints and structural properties into two tractable sequential search phases.
layout: 4 stages, left-to-right then down, thick arrows with transition labels, complexity badges
description: A flow diagram of four rounded boxes joined by thick navy block arrows. A blue box at the top left, 'Full Architectural Space, 16 dimensions (all MoE hyperparameters)', leads down-right to a gray 'Reduced Space, 14 dimensions' box. The arrow label reads 'Classical (C, M, D) scaling laws, Eliminate C, D'. An arrow then goes up-right to a green 'Core Search Space, 4 dimensions: (M, Na, N, d)'. Its label reads 'Fix 6 hardware/engineering params + 4 algebraic constraints'. A circular badge on the green box reads O(n^16) → O(n^4). A final arrow goes down-right, labeled 'Rank-preserving property of d', to a yellow box. The yellow box holds 'Phase 1: optimal (M, Na, N) via d-proxy' with an O(n^3) badge, and 'Phase 2: optimal d given (M, Na, N)' with an O(n^2) badge. The eye goes first to the blue box at top left, then follows the arrows to the yellow box.
caption: Overview of the dimension reduction pipeline. Starting from the full 16-dimensional MoE architectural space, we systematically reduce the search complexity to two sequential phases of O(n3) and O(n2) through classical scaling laws, algebraic constraints, engineering fixations, and the rank-preserving property of d.
abstract: Scaling laws govern macroscopic resource allocation for LLMs, yet precise architectural configurations for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models remain guided by heuristics. Existing MoE scaling studies either incorporate MoE-specific variables into scaling formulas, causing fitted coefficients to grow rapidly without proportional experimental support, or fix all non-MoE factors, implicitly assuming global architecture does not influence local MoE scaling. We propose a reusable framework for holistic MoE architectural optimization. We first show that MoE architectures decouple FLOPs per token ($M$), active parameters ($N_a$), and total parameters ($N$), which serve as distinct proxies for computation, weight access, and parameter storage. We therefore establish a joint constraint triad of $M$, active parameters ($N_a$), and total parameters ($N$) for rigorous MoE characterization. To tame the resulting $O(n^{16})$ search space, we employ mathematical decoupling: structural constraints and a rank-preserving property of the hidden dimension factorize the optimization into an $O(n^3) + O(n^2)$ two-phase search. Through extensive validation across 670+ MoE models spanning $10^{18}$ to $3 \times 10^{20}$ FLOPs, we derive globally applicable scaling laws mapping any compute budget to its optimal architecture. A key finding is that the near-optimal configuration band widens with scale, providing a quantitative basis for trade-offs between scaling law recommendations and engineering constraints. Our work delivers actionable blueprints for optimal MoE design under arbitrary compute budgets.
